evidence.criterion: failing tool mid-task: brain records the failure, recovers, completes; the tool's garbage never reaches state or saved files
evidence.note: Coordinator integration fix (Phase 7 gate): this experiment FAILED on the first Phase 7 tree for two reasons, both fixed in ab/brain.py. (1) Recovery stall: the flaky cut failed once at cycle 7, which banned (cut, situation); every replan then started with press (cheapest), press failed a second time, and the cut-first alternative was rejected because cut 'repeats a retrieved failure in the same situation' (the one flaky failure, which would succeed on retry) -- so the brain looped press-fail-replan until give_up_when_stalled. The fix: an alternative's first step is rejected only after >= 2 retrieved failures in the same situation (ADR P7-9), and the whole-sequence ban check now governs later steps only. (2) Garbage leak: the tool's raw error text was recorded as the episode surprise value, so learner.json carried the marker. The fix: a failed tool records only a typed surprise ('tool', 'failure'/'timeout'/'cancelled', tool-name) in its episode; the raw text stays in the events / tool audit, where failure records belong. (3) Three further defects in the same recovery path, found by tracing after (1)-(2) landed: (3a) the repeated-mistake swap in _do_make_plan was BLIND -- it swapped plans[0]/[1] unconditionally, undoing the relaxation sort that had already put the cut-first alternative on top, and re-adopted the twice-failed press-first plan. The swap is now conditional (only when plans[0] starts with the failed action) and the alternative_preferred event fires when the preference is honoured without a swap, too. (3b) The first attempt at a fix here -- narrowing _check_predictions to drop a plan only when its NEXT step depended on the violated effect -- was REVERTED: it broke three pinned Phase 2/5 tests (the SurpriseWorld prediction-confidence timing and the env_change interruption path), because the Phase 5 design drops a plan that still relies on the violated action anywhere, and the drop costs exactly one replan-only cycle. The drop stands; the recovery instead comes from (3c). (3c) the P4-9 relaxation fallback returned raw cost order when every candidate started with a banned retry -- but cost is order-independent, so it kept re-adopting press-first over cut-first. The fallback is now ordered by first-step failure rate, then failure COUNT, then cost: the rate alone cannot tell 1/1 from 3/3 (both 1.0), but the count can -- one failure is weak evidence (flaky), three consistent failures are strong. rlimit_cpu_burner.detail: exitcode -9 (SIGKILL); sandbox does not label the cause — attributed to the kernel's RLIMIT_CPU enforcement by elimination (no parent kill, no wall-time timeout; tool still burning CPU)

sidecar.method: CPU-burner tool (unbounded busy loop) run in the isolated subprocess path (ab.body.sandbox.IsolatedToolRunner, cpu_seconds=2, wall timeout 30s). Two burner runs plus a fast-tool control in the same runner. killed=False means the PARENT did not kill the child (the runner sets killed only when its own wall-time kill fires); exitcode -9 is the kernel's RLIMIT_CPU enforcement — soft and hard limits are equal (2s), so the kernel sends SIGXCPU and SIGKILL together and SIGKILL terminates the process. The sandbox reports only the exit code; it does not label the cause. Attribution rests on elimination: no parent kill, no wall-time timeout (timed_out=False, timeout 30s), and the tool was still burning CPU when it died.
